concepts.evidence: MiKaDiv XSD (ThirdPartyDisclosureRequest.xsd): FirstName EN "The person's first name." / DE "Vorname der Person." KaFE XSD (kafe-standardtypes.xsd, NatP_Struct): Vorname EN "First and middle name" / DE "Vorname". Kommunikationshandbuch DIP-KAFE confirms KaFE's field text is "Vorname [1..1] X First and middle name. The length must not exceed 80 characters." -- i.e. KaFE's field is explicitly documented to also carry middle names, not just a single first name. MiKaDiv's own handbook is silent on middle names ("mandatory details are the date of birth, last name and first name") but does not restrict the field to a single name either, and both schemas expose exactly one combined name field with no separate slot for additional given names -- so both fields cover the same real-world scope (the complete set of a person's given names, in whatever order/count they have them), making this exactMatch rather than closeMatch. Confirmed also to hold, verbatim, for KaFE's Ansprechperson_Struct.Vorname (contact person) -- identical EN/DE documentation text to NatP_Struct.Vorname.

MiKaDiv XSD: LastName EN "The person's last name." / DE "Nachname (Familienname) der Person." KaFE XSD (NatP_Struct): Nachname EN "Last name" / DE "Nachname". Both single-valued, no multi-value/ordering ambiguity (unlike given names) -- clean exactMatch. Confirmed also to hold, verbatim, for KaFE's Ansprechperson_Struct.Nachname (contact person) -- identical EN/DE documentation text to NatP_Struct.Nachname.
